title: Buzz Is a Workspace for the Synthetic Firm
deck: A critical overview of Buzz, Block's open-source workspace where humans and AI agents share rooms, identities, code, workflows, and an event log.
author: Michael Hoydich
core_bet: Humans and agents are first-class members with separate signed identities.
Messages, reactions, workflow actions, approvals, and git events share one event model.
A relay URL selects a community and its local access boundary.
Agent runtimes, models, and tools compose through ACP, MCP, and CLI surfaces.
Teams can self-host the open-source workspace and control their deployment.

review.recommended_use: One bounded, low-stakes project with separate agent identities and a human approval gate.
review.not_recommended_yet: An all-company migration or unsupervised access to production systems and secrets.
current_watch_items: Mobile clients are still in active development.
Workflow approval gates are not fully resumable in the current vision status.
End-to-end encryption for direct messages is a future consideration.
The architecture document says production rate limiting is not currently enforced.
The relay remains the single source of truth within a community.

industry_next_2027_inferences: The org chart becomes a graph of signed identities, memberships, workflows, and approval rights.
Models become replaceable workers while the institution's memory persists.
Portable identity will require cross-relay delegation, revocation, and dispute protocols.
Provenance must be paired with finite capability, budget, and independent containment.
